title: A Covered Bridge Visit
description: Look over an old-fashioned covered bridge through its timber, roof, supports, and crossing route.
cardDescription: Look over an old-fashioned covered bridge through its timber, roof, supports, and crossing route.
focus: A covered bridge encloses the roadway structure with a roof and sides. The clues describe parts of a traditional timber crossing without requiring a construction drawing.
solvingTip: Separate a part carrying the load from a part sheltering it. Short river and road words help with the structural terms.
words: Framework of connected members supporting many covered bridges
Large wood pieces used in a traditional bridge frame
Entrance opening at the end of a covered bridge
Upper covering sheltering a bridge's timber structure
Structure carrying a route over a river or gap
Surface that carries traffic across a bridge
Flowing water often crossed by a covered bridge
Upright support in a wooden structure
Vehicle route passing through a bridge
Land beside a waterway at the end of a crossing
Scene visible from beside a bridge
Fibrous tree material used in bridge carpentry

answerNotes.TRUSS: A truss supports loads through a connected framework. The roof is a different part covering the structure.
answerNotes.TIMBER: Timber is the structural wood. It names a material rather than the complete bridge.
answerNotes.PORTAL: The portal is the entrance opening. It is not the entire length of the crossing.
answerNotes.ROOF: A roof protects parts of a covered bridge from weather. Its purpose is separate from carrying the roadway load.
answerNotes.SPAN: A span is the section between supports. A bridge can have one span or several.

title: Inside a Lighthouse Museum
description: Explore a lighthouse through its beacon, optical parts, and the objects associated with its keeper.
cardDescription: Explore a lighthouse through its beacon, optical parts, and the objects associated with its keeper.
focus: The clues describe historical lighting and the tower around it. Different lighthouses used different light sources; the puzzle names equipment rather than a current navigation signal.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for a whole structure, a light-making part, or a person. Short lamp words help cross longer names.
words: Coastal tower carrying a light to guide vessels
Surname attached to a famous segmented lighthouse lens
Optical glass element used to direct a lighthouse beam
Person traditionally responsible for tending a lighthouse
Light or signal serving as a navigational guide
Glazed chamber at the top of many lighthouse towers
Tall structure raising a coastal light above its surroundings
Series of steps leading upward inside a lighthouse
Visible illumination sent toward the sea
Land bordering the sea near a lighthouse
Steep rock face on which a coastal tower may stand
Enclosed space within a lighthouse station
Fuel used in some historical lighthouse lamps
Fiber strip drawing lamp fuel toward a flame
Brief burst in a light's repeated signal pattern

answerNotes.LIGHTHOUSE: A lighthouse carries a navigational light. The museum setting does not imply the building is still operating with its original equipment.
answerNotes.FRESNEL: A Fresnel lens uses stepped sections to redirect light while reducing bulk. The name recalls Augustin-Jean Fresnel.
answerNotes.LENS: A lens changes the path of light. It is separate from the lamp that produces the light.
answerNotes.KEEPER: A keeper cared for the light and station. Many modern lights operate without a resident keeper.
answerNotes.BEACON: A beacon is a guiding signal. The tower is the structure that may carry it.

title: At the Old Schoolhouse Museum
description: Explore a preserved classroom through familiar writing tools, books, and everyday objects.
cardDescription: Explore a preserved classroom through familiar writing tools, books, and everyday objects.
focus: This is a museum scene rather than a school worksheet. The clues identify objects used in some earlier classrooms without suggesting that every school used the same furnishings.
solvingTip: Look for a writing surface, a teaching object, or a room fitting. Familiar short words can help with the older classroom terms.
words: Small reusable writing board used in some earlier classrooms
Soft writing material used on a classroom board
Introductory reading book used by a beginning reader
Small container supplying ink for a dipping pen
Heating appliance found in some one-room schoolhouses
Work surface at which a pupil could sit
Ringing instrument used to mark a school session
Unit of teaching prepared for a class
Book containing texts used for reading practice
To give the letters of a written word in order
Writing implement dipped into an ink supply
Drawing of places displayed for geography lessons
Bound printed volume kept on a classroom shelf
Ordered set of letters used in a writing system

answerNotes.SLATE: A writing slate could be cleaned and reused. Its material and purpose differ from a printed workbook.
answerNotes.CHALK: Chalk leaves a mark on a board. It is the writing material rather than the board itself.
answerNotes.PRIMER: Primer is a book word here. The same spelling can name a preparatory paint coating in another setting.
answerNotes.INKWELL: An inkwell holds writing fluid. It is separate from a pen's point or the paper receiving the marks.
answerNotes.STOVE: A stove could heat a classroom. The clue asks for the appliance, not the fuel burned in it.

title: Shelves in a General Store
description: Visit a traditional general-store scene through bulk goods, containers, and the counter where purchases were recorded.
cardDescription: Visit a traditional general-store scene through bulk goods, containers, and the counter where purchases were recorded.
focus: The clues identify old-fashioned retail objects rather than brand names or historical prices. A selling container and the goods inside it have different names.
solvingTip: Look for a container, a measuring object, or a written record. Short packaging words can help with the longer store fittings.
words: Large curved-sided wooden container used for bulk store goods
Roll or folded length of cloth sold from a store counter
Bowl-shaped utensil used to transfer loose store goods
Raised shop surface where purchases are handled
Cloth sold by length in a general store
Device used to weigh bulk goods before sale
Strong open container used to transport store supplies
Rigid container storing small goods or food
Removable top on a storage container
Metal container for a store's packaged goods
Cleaning product stocked beside other household supplies

answerNotes.BARREL: A barrel is a container in this clue. It is not the hitting section of a baseball bat.
answerNotes.BOLT: A bolt of fabric is a commercial length of cloth. It is different from a threaded metal fastener.
answerNotes.LEDGER: A ledger holds financial records. It differs from a list of the store's opening hours or the labels on its shelves.
answerNotes.SCOOP: A scoop moves loose goods from a bin. It names the utensil rather than one fixed unit of weight.
answerNotes.COUNTER: A counter is the retail work surface. It is not a person or device that counts in this clue.

title: An Evening at the Drive-In
description: Explore a drive-in movie through parked cars, the outdoor screen, and the equipment used to show a feature.
cardDescription: Explore a drive-in movie through parked cars, the outdoor screen, and the equipment used to show a feature.
focus: This scene concerns watching a film from a vehicle. Older speaker arrangements and radio sound both appear in the vocabulary; individual theaters can use different systems.
solvingTip: Separate the picture-making equipment from the sound equipment and the parking space. Short setting words help with the longer theater terms.
words: Machine casting a film's images onto a drive-in screen
Sound-producing device traditionally hung beside some drive-in cars
Small enclosed room housing a cinema's projection equipment
Word completing ___ feature, a program of two movies
Open area where drive-in viewers park their vehicles
Large outdoor surface on which a drive-in movie is shown
Road vehicle in which a drive-in viewer sits
Line of parked vehicles facing an outdoor screen
Admission record for a drive-in showing
Main film in a cinema program
Small food item bought during a movie outing
Flat support holding a drive-in meal or refreshments
Car receiver used for sound at some drive-in theaters
Evening period when daylight is fading

answerNotes.PROJECTOR: A projector makes the displayed image. It is separate from the speaker or radio carrying the soundtrack.
answerNotes.SPEAKER: Some older drive-ins used individual speakers. Others use radio transmission, so the clue describes a traditional arrangement.
answerNotes.BOOTH: A projection booth houses equipment. It differs from a concession counter selling food.
answerNotes.DOUBLE: A double feature presents two films. The term describes the program rather than two seats in one car.
answerNotes.LOT: A lot is a parking area here. It does not describe a large quantity.
